venue.name: Chemainus Theatre Festival
venue.description: The Chemainus Theatre Festival is a professional non-profit theatre in the seaside village of Chemainus, on the Cowichan coast. It puts on a mainstage season of five plays a year, with matinees at 2:00 pm and evening shows Wednesday through Sunday. Groups of ten or more adults get 15 percent off tickets, anyone 18 and under gets 50 percent off premium and standard seats, and a small number of free tickets are set aside each season for educational and community organisations. The site publishes no theatre school, backstage tour or classroom workshop, so what a class books here is a seat at a performance.

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: An elevator is available to access the upper level of the theatre and the Playbill Dining Room. Designated accessible seating is available for those using wheelchairs, walkers, or attending with a service dog.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Bus and RV parking are available on Croft St, a few blocks away from the theatre.

restrictions: Children under the age of 4 are not admitted to Mainstage performances, except for Relaxed Performances or KidzPlay shows
Children must have a ticket and sit with a parent or guardian
Only non-alcoholic beverages are permitted in the theatre auditorium
In consideration of others, we ask our guests to refrain from wearing scented products
All tickets are non-refundable. Tickets can be exchanged for another date with at least 24 hours' notice
venue.hours_notes: Box Office open Tuesday to Friday 10 AM to 4 PM and Saturday 10 AM to 2 PM, plus 2 hours before each performance for in-person sales. Closed on statutory holidays.
venue.seasonal_notes: The 2026 season runs from 20 February to 23 December. Godspell 20 February to 29 March, The Ladies Foursome 17 April to 17 May, Dirty Rotten Scoundrels 12 June to 23 August, Peril in the Alps 25 September to 25 October, The Wickhams: Christmas at Pemberley 13 November to 23 December. There are no performances in January.

programs.name: Group booking for a mainstage performance
programs.description: A block booking for a group at one of the five mainstage plays. Groups of 10 or more adults get 15 percent off, and one free ticket comes with 20 or more tickets. Anyone 18 and under gets 50 percent off premium and standard seats, and post-secondary students get 40 percent off with student ID. The 2026 group rates start at $49 per person for theatre only in standard seating, rising to $61 per person for Dirty Rotten Scoundrels and The Wickhams. Those are starting prices for adults and include GST and fees. Matinees are at 2:00 pm on Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday. A buffet lunch, brunch or dinner in the Playbill Dining Room can be added for an extra charge.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the auditorium and watch a professional play. There is an intermission part way through when they can get out of their seats and into the lobby.
programs.our_note: This is a show, not a workshop, so the children sit and watch for the whole thing. Every published discount is written either for adults or for individual youth tickets, so ask the group coordinator how a class of children is counted before you set your budget.
programs.practical_summary: Coach parking is a few blocks away on Croft St, and inside there is a lift and reserved accessible seating. Whether there is anywhere to eat a packed lunch is not stated, and neither is anything about the toilets, so both are worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Group prices include a $2 Capital Improvement Fee and 5% GST. There is a $3.15 service fee on all theatre tickets. A 15% gratuity per person is added if you dine in the Playbill Dining Room.
programs.payment_timing: A 10% deposit is required at the time of booking, with a minimum deposit of $50 for groups of 20 tickets or less. A due date for the final payment is set when you book.
programs.cancellation_note: The deposit will be refunded if cancellation is received 30 days prior to the performance date. An administration fee of $50 will be charged if cancellation is received after the 30-day deadline. The deposit becomes non-refundable if full payment is not received by the final payment date.
programs.evidence: 15% discount off theatre tickets for groups of 10 adults or more

programs.name: BMO Relaxed Performance
programs.description: A performance run in a deliberately casual way. House lights stay partly on, sudden sounds and effects are reduced, and the audience may move about, make noise and leave and come back. The theatre says these are a good option for anyone with small children and for people with Tourette, Parkinson's and Autism Spectrum Disorder. The usual minimum age of 4 does not apply. All Relaxed Performances are Pay What You Can and are only bookable by phoning the Box Office. The 2026 dates are 26 February, 23 April, 18 June, 1 October and 19 November, all Thursdays at 2:00 PM.
programs.what_children_do: Watch a professional play in a room where the lights stay partly on, and where they are allowed to move, make noise, and go out and come back in.
programs.our_note: You set the price yourself when you phone, which makes this the cheapest way in for a group on a tight budget. Only the October and November dates are still ahead this season, and both are Thursday afternoons.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors, with a lift and reserved accessible seating, and the theatre says movement and noise are fine at these shows. Toilets and anywhere to eat a packed lunch are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Pay What You Can, so you choose the price. There is a $3.15 service fee on all theatre tickets.
programs.evidence: All Relaxed Performances are Pay-What-You-Can, available by calling the Box Office at 1-800-565-7738.

programs.name: Access Tickets for schools and community groups
programs.description: Free tickets for organisations working with people who face financial, social, cultural or physical barriers to attending live theatre. Educational organisations and community and social services organisations are both eligible. Apply at least two weeks before the performance you want, naming the exact date and production. A maximum of 10 tickets per group is considered, subject to availability, and an organisation may receive tickets for up to two productions a season. Priority goes to organisations that have not been to the Chemainus Theatre before. The theatre says it replies within two to three business days.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the auditorium and watch a professional play, with an intermission part way through when they can get out of their seats.
programs.our_note: Ten tickets is the ceiling, so this covers a small group rather than a whole class. Apply at least two weeks out and name the exact performance, and count on it being a request rather than a booking until they reply.
programs.practical_summary: Same building as any other performance, so there is a lift, reserved accessible seating and coach parking a few blocks away. Toilets and lunch space are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
programs.cancellation_note: Access Tickets have no cash value and must be accepted as awarded.
programs.evidence: A maximum of 10 tickets per group will be considered, based on availability

gaps: No school matinees, student matinee rate, theatre school, drama classes, backstage tours or classroom workshops are advertised anywhere on the site. What a class can book here is a seat at a public performance. If a schools programme exists it is not published.

KidzPlay is named twice as an exception to the minimum age of 4, but no KidzPlay show appears in the 2026 season listing or the season calendar, and there is no KidzPlay page on the site. Worth asking whether it still runs.

Price for a child in a group: unknown. Youth 18 and under get 50 percent off premium and standard seats, but the group rate sheet is written for adults only and no dollar figure for a child in a group is published. The $49 recorded is the adult starting price for theatre only in standard seating.
Washrooms: not mentioned anywhere on the site.
Somewhere for a group to eat a packed lunch: not mentioned. The Playbill Dining Room and the concession are both paid food service.
How many adults have to come with a group of children: not stated.
How long a performance runs, including the interval: not stated for any 2026 show.
Minimum notice for a group booking: not stated. Only the Access Ticket scheme gives a lead time, which is two weeks.
Whether a group of children can be given the group discount at all: the discount is written as 10 or more adults, and it is not clear how a school or daycare group is treated.
Buggy access: not stated. There is a lift and accessible seating, but nothing about pushchairs.

Ticket checkout, seat selection and the live price table all sit on the theatre's separate ticketing system at purchase.chemainustheatrefestival.ca. We did not extract from it. Prices here come from the group rate sheet and the season calendar published on the main site.
The group ticket request link on the group bookings page points at a Microsoft Forms page off the theatre's own site. We recorded the on-site request form instead.

The address is published in the footer of every page. The coordinates come from the Google Maps place links the theatre publishes on its own FAQ and accessibility pages, which give 48.9212376, -123.7171703 and 48.9212321, -123.717156 respectively. The two are about six metres apart and we used the first.
The performance format does not fit any of the four values the app allows for how a session runs, so that field was left empty.

values: $3.15 service fee on all theatre tickets
conflicts.note: Two of their pages give a different booking fee on each ticket. One says $3.00 and the other says $3.15. It is small money, but multiply it by a class and ask the box office which figure they are charging.
